source.title: RA$^2$: Retain-Anchored Attraction Preserves Forget-Adjacent Utility in LLM Unlearning
source.authors: Zi-Nan Ling; Yang Xiao; Rui-Meng Ye; Si-Jia Liu; Bo Hui

record.tranche_reason: The paper tests post-training quantization on an unlearned model and reports that forgetting remains close to the unquantized result, challenging substantial recovery by quantization in the tested setting.
record.gate_note: Rows are limited to the paper's own post-training quantization results on WMDP forgetting. The paper also reports adjacent-utility, unlearning, and direction-sweep results, but these do not test the specified fine-tuning, activation-ablation, or prompt-rephrasing recovery claims. Cited robustness results are not counted.
record.test_reason: The paper applies post-training int8 and NF4 quantization to its new RA2 unlearned Zephyr-7B-β and reports WMDP-Bio/Cyber accuracy before and after. This is a direct result on whether quantization restores forgotten knowledge, and on whether a newer method resists that attack. It is a new method and setting, not a reproduction of an original source, so T3 fits better than T5.
record.authors_conclusion: Essentially correct. The authors state that 8-bit and NF4 compression keep RA2 close to its unquantized operating point on WMDP, MMLU and MMLU-Perturbed, so the retain-anchored direction is not a fragile full-precision artifact. Their main conclusion, however, concerns forget-adjacent utility, not robustness to recovery.
record.recipe_differences: RA2 is a new latent-space unlearning method that redirects forget-token states toward retain anchors; the quantization experiment applies post-training compression to RA2 rather than reproducing the unlearning and recovery procedures in the cited original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: The tested quantization formats produce slightly different WMDP scores; nf4_bnb lowers Bio accuracy slightly and raises Cyber accuracy, while int8_bnb raises both relative to the unquantized reference.
record.problems: The quantization table reports point values without error bars. This robustness check covers RA2 and two quantization formats only; it does not test recovery attacks such as fine-tuning, activation ablation, or prompting.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant quantization rows omitted. Other reported results do not measure recovery by one of the specified attack types.

untested.parts: Only one attack (quantization) is applied to the unlearned model. Fine-tuning, activation ablation and jailbreak attacks are not tested, so the full claim that simple attacks don't recover the knowledge is not tested.
No relearning or fine-tuning attack on any unlearned model.
No direction ablation or probing of whether knowledge is blocked rather than deleted. The direction sweeps are training-objective variants, not recovery attacks.
Quantization is applied only to RA2, not to GA, NPO, RMU or the other baselines. Only bitsandbytes int8 and NF4 are tested, on Zephyr only.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or adversarial in-context attacks. Only a benign MMLU prefix before WMDP questions is tested (Table 11).
RA2's resistance is tested only against quantization, not fine-tuning, ablation or prompting attacks.

missing.what: Suppression under a benign MMLU prefix before WMDP targets. Bio/Cyber: RMU 27.7/27.7, RMU-LAT 31.3/31.2, RA2 29.6/25.3, versus original 62.3/40.7. This is a mild context change that does not restore the knowledge; it is not an adversarial prompt.
MMLU and MMLU-Perturbed after quantization (int8 0.5615/0.5702, nf4 0.5575/0.5692 vs 0.5660/0.5570). This shows utility is preserved alongside the WMDP rows.

record.verdict_notes: Quantization is a secondary robustness check on the authors' own method. No baseline is quantized, so the study cannot show where quantization does restore knowledge. The unquantized reference (Bio 0.2930) differs slightly from the 10-seed mean (0.2983), so the quantization shifts are within roughly seed-level variation. The paper cites Zhang et al. (arXiv:2410.16454) for quantization recovery but does not reproduce its GA/NPO setting.

versions.untested_parts: The paper measures direct forgetting and broad utility for unlearning methods, but does not test whether the knowledge is recoverable through the specified attacks; it therefore does not test this full claim version.
Recovery by fine-tuning on unrelated, loosely related, or subset examples.
Recovery by activation-direction ablation, or evidence that a tested method blocks access rather than deleting knowledge.
The paper tests int8_bnb and nf4_bnb quantization on RA2; it does not test quantization on the other unlearning methods.
Recovery through rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information.
RA2 is tested for quantization robustness only; resistance to fine-tuning, activation ablation, and prompting attacks is not tested.

rows.subject: Zephyr-7B-β RA2
rows.operation_detail: Post-training int8_bnb quantization of RA2 weights.
rows.measure: WMDP-Bio accuracy (lower is better for forgetting)
rows.note: The small increase is in the direction of recovery, but the authors say quantized results remain close to the unquantized operating point.
rows.check: Bio rises 0.2930→0.2985 (+0.55 pt) against an original-model 63.7 and chance ~25. The authors call this close to the unquantized point, which is negligible recovery, so absent rather than partial.

rows.subject: Zephyr-7B-β RA2
rows.operation_detail: Post-training int8_bnb quantization of RA2 weights.
rows.measure: WMDP-Cyber accuracy (lower is better for forgetting)
rows.note: The modest increase is in the direction of recovery, but the authors characterize quantized results as remaining close to the unquantized reference.
rows.check: Cyber rises 0.2730→0.2828 (+1 pt) against an original 44.0. The authors describe it as close to the reference, so absent rather than partial.

rows.subject: Zephyr-7B-β RA2
rows.operation_detail: Post-training nf4_bnb quantization of RA2 weights.
rows.measure: WMDP-Bio accuracy (lower is better for forgetting)
rows.note: WMDP-Bio accuracy is slightly lower than the unquantized reference, so this result does not indicate recovery.
rows.check: Bio falls slightly, 0.2930→0.2899. A 0.3 pt drop is no recovery, not an opposite effect worth calling reversed, so absent.

rows.subject: Zephyr-7B-β RA2
rows.operation_detail: Post-training nf4_bnb quantization of RA2 weights.
rows.measure: WMDP-Cyber accuracy (lower is better for forgetting)
rows.note: The increase is in the direction of recovery but remains a small change relative to the much higher original-model WMDP-Cyber accuracy reported in Table 3.
rows.check: Cyber rises 0.2730→0.2929 (+2 pt, about 12% of the gap to the original 44.0). This is a small move toward recovery, so partial is acceptable. These are single runs with no error bars; the 10-seed std for RA2 Cyber is ±0.0033.

source_check.problem: Borderline: the authors call all quantized results close to the reference, so absent is also defensible. Partial is acceptable for +2 pt, about 12% of the gap to 44.0.

relationships.condition: RA2 (retain-anchored latent unlearning) on Zephyr-7B-β, int8_bnb and nf4_bnb post-training quantization, WMDP-Bio/Cyber
relationships.reason: Quantization leaves WMDP near chance: Bio 29.3→29.9/29.0 and Cyber 27.3→28.3/29.3, versus original 63.7/44.0 (R1–R4). Recovery by quantization does not occur for this method.
relationships.display_finding: Bio accuracy changed from 29.3 to 29.9 or 29.0 and Cyber from 27.3 to 28.3 or 29.3, remaining far below original scores of 63.7 and 44.0.

relation.reason: The paper reports its own quantization results on WMDP, which bear on versions D and F.

tranche.reason: A new method (RA2) is tested under quantization, which gives a result on versions D and F in a new setting. The paper makes no argument that a version is wrong, so T5 does not fit.

source_check.notes: Quantization appears only in Table 8 and Table 15 (same numbers). Neither table names the model; Zephyr-7B-β is inferred from MMLU 0.5660 (Table 3 RA2: Zephyr 56.6, Qwen3 66.6). There are no error bars or seed counts. The unquantized reference (0.2930/0.2730) differs from the 10-seed RA2 means (0.2983/0.2924). Only RA2 is quantized, and no other recovery attack is run.

statements.correction: Add RA2 (Zephyr-7B-β, authors' own test): WMDP-Bio 0.2930->0.2985 (int8_bnb), 0.2899 (nf4_bnb); WMDP-Cyber 0.2730->0.2828, 0.2929; original 63.7/44.0. Or drop the citation.
statements.problem: Cites R1-R3 from this study but never names RA2 or gives its numbers. Its general claim (little or no recovery, tested only by the method's own authors) does fit R1-R3.

statements.correction: RA2: Bio int8 0.2985, nf4 0.2899; Cyber int8 0.2828, nf4 0.2929; unquantized 0.2930/0.2730. The authors say both formats stay close to the unquantized reference.
statements.problem: The numbers are right (0.2985 and 0.2899 as 29.9 and 29.0). But RA2 is given as an example of bnb formats differing. For RA2, int8 and nf4 differ by under 1 pt on Bio, the order reverses on Cyber, and the authors call both close to the unquantized reference.

statements.correction: RA2 is a latent-space method for forget-adjacent utility. The authors' only recovery test is post-training int8_bnb/nf4_bnb quantization, with no error bars or seeds. Bio 0.2930->0.2985/0.2899; Cyber 0.2730->0.2828/0.2929; MMLU 0.5660->0.5615/0.5575.
statements.problem: The RA2 numbers are right. But RA2 was not built against quantization: it targets forget-adjacent utility, and quantization is a robustness check (Table 8, Table 15). The quantization table has no error bars or seed count, so 'uncertainty' does not cover this test. 'Tested only against it' is right: no other recovery attack is run.

statements.correction: Add RA2 (Zephyr-7B-β): int8_bnb vs nf4_bnb give nearly the same WMDP accuracy: Bio 0.2985 vs 0.2899, Cyber 0.2828 vs 0.2929 (unquantized 0.2930/0.2730). Or drop the citation.
statements.problem: Cites R1-R4 from this study but gives no RA2 content. RA2 shows almost no bit-width effect, unlike the 4-bit-worse pattern the statement lists.

reader_labels.reason: Quantization leaves forgetting close to the unquantized reference rather than restoring most targeted knowledge; the modest increases are in R1, R2, and R4, while R3 moves in the opposite direction.
